items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: I called him, I said Foots, let's try to make an arrangement on this and call it 'Ratamacue' and he sit up there and we did it.

ctx.x: Yeah, Foots Thomas is the one got me on the band. And I didn't want to join the band first because I was having a ball over there on 52nd Street with Stuff. Stuff Smith, small band, and of course, with Cab's band, Cab and Duke then were the highest paid bands out there, which was $100 a week, but see with Cab I was getting $150 and so was Chu. See we were featured members of the band so we made $150 apiece, but the top salary then was really $100 a week. Cab and Duke was the only ones that could afford to pay…
Did you get any expenses taken out in addition to the salary.

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: No, Walter Thomas got me on the band, Foots. ... Walter Thomas was upstairs while I was practicing. And I called him, I said Foots, let's try to make an arrangement on this and call it 'Ratamacue' and he sit up there and we did it.

ctx.x: And yourself. And those titles are "Each Day," "If Someone Would Only Love Me," "That Will Never Do," and "I'm Looking for a Little Bluebird." And the second session which is June 2, 1930, is Jelly Roll, again Ward Pinkett and another on trumpet, Geechie Fields on trombone, Happy Caldwell on clarinet, Joe Thomas on alto sax, Walter Thomas on clarinet and baritone, Lee Blair on banjo, Billy Taylor once again on bass, and you; and those are "Oil Well," two takes of "Load of Coal," and "Crazy Chords," and "Primrose…
Yeah, "Primrose Stomp." It rings a bell.
